sourceMethod: Official U.S. and allied documents; curated summaries distinguish allegations from assessments

russian-cyber.title: Russian state-linked cyber operations
russian-cyber.summary: Published U.S. and allied records describe GRU-linked cyber operations targeting Ukrainian systems, defense contractors and global networks. These records support concrete historical findings and a 2026 disruption, not an assertion that any particular organization is currently compromised.
russian-cyber.why: Cyber operations can intersect with military conflict, stolen defense technology, infrastructure resilience and information security. Separate Unit 29155 activity from GRU Unit 26165/APT28 and separate law-enforcement charges from intelligence assessments.
russian-cyber.uncertainty: No verified live attack count, victims or forecast is supplied here. Criminal charges remain allegations unless an independently verified judicial outcome is linked.

evidence.title: Russian GRU Unit 29155 targeted critical infrastructure
evidence.finding: U.S. and allied agencies assess that GRU Unit 29155 ran espionage, sabotage and destructive cyber operations. The advisory describes the WhisperGate campaign against Ukrainian organizations and activity involving global infrastructure.

evidence.title: Russian state-sponsored targeting of cleared defense contractors
evidence.finding: U.S. agencies reported regular targeting of defense contractors from January 2020 to February 2022, seeking sensitive defense-related information and technology. The date range is historical.

evidence.title: GRU Unit 26165 / APT28 router hijacking disruption
evidence.finding: DOJ reported a U.S. operation addressing compromised small-office and home routers used for DNS hijacking and intelligence collection. This involves GRU Unit 26165/APT28, which is distinct from Unit 29155.

evidence.title: GRU Unit 29155 cyber case — indictment announcement
evidence.finding: DOJ unsealed charges against five Russian GRU officers and one civilian in connection with alleged WhisperGate-related activity and targeting of countries supporting Ukraine.

china-cyber.title: PRC-linked cyber investigations and critical infrastructure warnings
china-cyber.summary: DOJ's 2025 release describes charged hacker-for-hire operations involving i-Soon and individuals connected with PRC agencies. Separately, CISA and partners described Volt Typhoon's potential infrastructure disruption risk.
china-cyber.why: The published materials document distinct espionage, data theft and critical-infrastructure concerns. They do not establish that every company or national of the PRC is implicated.
china-cyber.uncertainty: DOJ defendants are accused, not presumed guilty. Volt Typhoon is a distinct campaign; do not combine actor attributions.

evidence.title: PRC hacker-for-hire allegations involving i-Soon and officials
evidence.classification: Charges and indictments — allegations, not convictions
evidence.finding: DOJ announced charges against 12 PRC nationals, including public-security officers and individuals connected to i-Soon and APT27, alleging global intrusions and targeting of critics, organizations and government entities.

evidence.title: PRC Volt Typhoon critical infrastructure risk briefing
evidence.finding: U.S. agencies warned that PRC state-sponsored actors had pre-positioned in critical infrastructure networks, posing potential disruption risk in future geopolitical crises. This is a separate actor and case from the DOJ i-Soon allegations.

defense|Cyber operations.title: Cyber operations — official intelligence assessment
defense|Cyber operations.summary: Public U.S. government and allied assessments identify documented cyber campaigns associated with Russian military intelligence and PRC-linked actors. The dashboard previously linked only to CISA's homepage, which could not substantiate any specific case.
defense|Cyber operations.why: The evidence indicates why cyber intrusions matter for defense, industrial supply chains and critical infrastructure. Each campaign must retain its own attribution and publication date.
defense|Cyber operations.uncertainty: The specific records below concern different actor groups, countries and reporting periods. This is not a current global cyber incident feed.

assets|Space & cyber.title: Strategic space and cyber capability — evidence review
assets|Space & cyber.summary: The linked CISA source supplies cybersecurity assessments, not a comprehensive inventory of military satellites or current unit locations. Joint advisories document state-linked digital threats, while broader space capability analysis needs separate defense and space-agency reports.
assets|Space & cyber.why: Cyber access to defense contractors and critical infrastructure can affect communications, logistics and resilience; it does not itself quantify space-force capabilities.
assets|Space & cyber.uncertainty: No validated country-by-country force inventories or live military asset locations are claimed here.

cases|Chinese contract hackers & officia.title: DOJ case review — Chinese contract hackers and officials
cases|Chinese contract hackers & officia.summary: The Justice Department announced March 5, 2025 charges against 12 Chinese nationals in multiple computer-intrusion matters, including alleged involvement by i-Soon employees and government officers.
cases|Chinese contract hackers & officia.why: The cases illustrate alleged relationships between contractors, state agencies and private-sector hacking services; the published release links to separate indictments.
cases|Chinese contract hackers & officia.uncertainty: The release is not proof that every defendant was convicted. Court dispositions must be checked independently.

defense|Russia–Ukraine.title: Russia–Ukraine: strategic and cyber dimensions
defense|Russia–Ukraine.scope: War, cyber operations and defense consequences
defense|Russia–Ukraine.summary: Official records describe destructive malware targeting Ukrainian government networks in the run-up to the 2022 invasion, as well as subsequent cyber targeting of countries supporting Ukraine. These sources describe the cyber dimension, not the complete battlefield picture.
defense|Russia–Ukraine.why: Digital disruption can affect civilian systems and critical infrastructure and intersect with energy security and allied support.
defense|Russia–Ukraine.uncertainty: These sources do not establish current operational positions or the full status of the conflict on the present date.

providers.label: CISA
providers.scope: Cybersecurity advisories, exploited vulnerabilities and critical infrastructure guidance.
providers.limits: A catalog or vulnerability listing alone does not establish attacker attribution; use the individual advisory and its date.

providers.label: U.S. Department of Justice
providers.scope: Criminal charges, court records, public enforcement and national security cases.
providers.limits: A charge or indictment is an allegation; verify outcomes in court records.

providers.label: Foreign Agents Registration Act (DOJ)
providers.scope: Foreign-agent registrations, disclosures and related public filings.
providers.limits: Registration is a legal disclosure, not proof of illicit foreign influence.

providers.label: U.S. Treasury OFAC
providers.scope: Sanctions programs, designation notices and consolidated list metadata.
providers.limits: A designation is a legal sanctions status, not independent proof of every alleged activity.

providers.label: OFAC Sanctions Search
providers.scope: Searchable U.S. sanctions list records and aliases.
providers.limits: This search page is not a permanent individual-record permalink; check identifiers and update dates.

providers.label: U.S. Defense Department
providers.scope: Official military news, published strategic assessments and policy statements.
providers.limits: General news pages do not establish a specific military operation or a current asset position.

providers.label: U.S. defense news portal
providers.scope: Public defense reporting; confirm document title and date before treating as evidence.
providers.limits: A publisher's homepage alone does not support a country-specific operational claim.

providers.label: U.S. Central Command
providers.scope: Dated U.S. Central Command statements and public operational context.
providers.limits: Press-release indexes are not real-time tracking and may omit other perspectives.

providers.label: NATO
providers.scope: Alliance treaties, policy, public decisions and official statements.
providers.limits: Alliance membership does not imply involvement in an individual event.

providers.label: U.S. State Department
providers.scope: Diplomatic releases, country information, treaty and sanctions policy.
providers.limits: A departmental homepage is not a case-specific finding.

providers.label: Defense Security Cooperation Agency
providers.limits: A notification of a proposed sale is not evidence that equipment was delivered.

providers.label: World Bank
providers.scope: Country economic indicators and statistical series.
providers.limits: Data vintages differ, and economic membership does not imply a unified political or military posture.
